summary: A GitHub repository observer that resumes from another member's read position on a repository with more than 1,000 open issues and pull requests no longer fails every poll when reactions are not among its fields. It reads the open listing ten pages per poll until the listing ends. A plugin-database cursor written while the same observer is being forgotten is now dropped by the next forget.

replay.detail: No claim is written, rewritten or replayed.

schema.detail: No table or version change in the GitHub plugin database. The repository cursor stored there gains an optional resume_next (the open listing's next page). A build without it ignores the field, and the field never rides in a claim.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes, and no fleet coordination.

compatibility.detail: No claim, client, wire or harness contract change. Correction to github-cursor-followups: a resume reads the open listing on its first poll and, when the listing has more than ten pages, on the polls after it until the listing ends. Before this change, such a resume failed every poll with 'the GitHub listing has more than 10 pages'. Each continuation is one REST page read, inside the github-admission budget. Limits: the listing is paged by offset, so an item that closes between two polls can make the first item past a page boundary go unread until it next changes. An observer that also has the reactions field still fails on such a repository, because the open-reactions read is not resumable; that is unchanged here.

recovery.detail: Rolling back returns to a resume that fails on a repository with more than 1,000 open items. A resume_next left in a cursor is ignored.
